newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's ABA examines pay TV local content.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's ABA examines pay TV local content.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Tuesday it would examine the Australian content in the programming of the country's fledging pay TV operators.
Pay TV licensees are already subject to a condition that 10 percent of expenditure on channels devoted predominantly to drama must be on new Australian drama programmes.

"The investigation will examine the contributions the pay TV sector should be required to make in developing and reflecting a sense of Australian identity, character and cultural diversity," ABA chairman Peter Webb said in a statement.

Webb noted that while the ABA would be looking at fresh options, any extension of the current requirements would be examined in the light of capacity to pay and the production capacity of the Australian industry.
"The ABA will be developing options for varying or extending the current requirements and ways to encourage Australian content on pay TV," he said.
"A critical consideration will be the ability of the pay TV industry to finance such requirements and the capacity of the Australian production industry to produce the necessary programs."
The ABA said it would report to Communications Minister Richard Alston by April 30, 1997.
There are currently three pay TV services operating in Australia-Foxtel, Galaxy and Optus Vision.
Foxtel is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation Ltd and State-owned telecommunications group Telstra.
Galaxy is operated by Australis Media in which Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting and US group Lenfest Communications are major shareholders.

Optus Vision is 46.5 percent owned by telecommunications carrier Optus Communications, US-based Continental Cablevision also with 46.5 percent, Publishing and Broadcasting with five percent and Kerry Stoke's Seven Network with two percent.
